changes: Recognize dense revolution/invasion plans (at least12 cards) as nonsummon threats, while preserving the established invasion counter threshold. Do not confuse a hand change with deployment from graveyard or mana.

Against8 or more Chara/Koppi cost reducers, admit payable cheap bodies with unconditional entry removal. Ignore evolved-only entry, attack effects, self-removal and complex target filters for this role.
Retain40-card legality, color supply, overlap and support constraints. Existing generated-cache versioning rejectsv2 entries for lazy rebuilding without rewriting user decks or deleting saved data.

officialSources.supports: Skull reacts to nonsummon entry, not ordinary paid summons.
Val has revolution change and an entry ability. Native tests confirm the entry ability still resolves when Skull destroys Val.
Zaag has low-cost element removal on entry.
Shoma has low-cost element removal on entry.

baseline-matrix.method: Paired real opposing archetypes with recorded CPU lists. Opponent always uses the frozen baseline AI. Build and CPU turn policy are selected independently; compare targetCaseHash for builder comparisons and caseHash when decks must also match. Physical80-card identities checked after every action. Each isolated case has a60-second process safety limit; game rules and AI decisions never use that wall clock.

comparison.interpretation: Both builders won10/12 primary games. Both won1/2 held-out revolution games, but the winning first-player cases swapped. The original two fresh-game losses remain. No overall fresh-game strength gain is established.

adaptation.method: Existing learnStrongestDefeat and previousBuild produce a legal next deck after each native defeat. Finalv3 native tests win the next game in both first-player conditions, conserve80 identities after every legal action and verify feedback invariance to hidden cards.
adaptation.note: The diagnostic report predates the cache-version bump. The finalv3 native tests repeat the two adaptation conditions successfully; this verifies existing learning rather than implementing new learning logic.

limitations: The original revolution cases still lose when starting without feedback. The held-out swap includes one improved and one worsened outcome; candidate recognition does not establish a general win-rate gain.
These counters do not prevent all ordinary summons or cancel already-triggered entry abilities.
Fixed-condition learned wins do not guarantee adaptation wins against every opponent or seed.
No deletion or migration of oldv2 caches or version-keyed learning was introduced. Cross-version learning reuse remains outside this change.
Historical full npm test remains interrupted/unconfirmed. Old broad long-running groups and full npm test were not rerun; previous pending items remain intact.
Each command has a570-second kill limit. Every comparison completed inside its60-second/1000-action/80-turn case limits.
